steps.title: Build listening comprehension for workplace conversations
steps.description: Follow and respond to spoken instructions the way they appear on the job: short conversations, task briefings and one-on-one check-ins. Practise with recordings or role plays and summarize what you heard.

steps.title: Practise speaking clearly in workplace settings
steps.description: Deliver short spoken updates and explain ideas out loud until they land: run a two-minute stand-up, phone back a customer, or explain a task to a teammate.

steps.title: Practise active listening with real conversations
steps.description: Paraphrase before you reply, ask one clarifying question per conversation, and confirm instructions back to the speaker. Ten deliberate minutes a day is enough to see the difference.

steps.title: Learn to evaluate options against criteria
steps.description: Take three real decisions from work or school, list what a good outcome requires, score each option against it, and write down why you chose the one you did.

steps.title: Practise breaking down a system into requirements
steps.description: Pick a tool or process you use every week, trace its inputs and outputs, and write the requirements a replacement would need. Repeat once with a bigger system.

steps.title: Learn to teach and demonstrate tasks to others
steps.description: Choose a task you know well and teach it twice: once as a spoken walkthrough, once as a written quick-start guide. Ask the learner what confused them and fix it.

steps.title: Practise presenting a convincing case
steps.description: For a change you want to make, prepare a one-page case: the problem, two options, costs and one recommendation. Deliver it to someone who can say no.

steps.title: Practise structured decision making
steps.description: Use a decision journal for a month: write the call you need to make, the deadline, the two best options and the outcome. Review it at the end of the month.

steps.title: Build a personal time management system
steps.description: Pick one system (time blocks, a task board, or a daily top-three list), run it for two weeks without skipping, and adjust at the end instead of mid-week.

steps.title: Find a project to build relevant experience
steps.description: Explore volunteer work, freelance projects, or a stretch task that lets you practise skills relevant to this career.

steps.title: Refresh your resume for this career
steps.description: Review job postings and highlight the relevant skills and experience you can demonstrate in your resume.

steps.title: Talk to people about this career
steps.description: Ask people in your network about their experience, career paths, and practical ways to learn more about this field.
